column8: Wed 18 Nov: 3e area 4 store; Taiwan's ten big public arts buildings from first approved total (median 31.6%, mean 42%, 8 of 10 above 25%, all reproduced); a landmark class, said in its own column, never an estimate of her building.

Wed 18 Nov: 3b/3e; register-backed count (24.9% and 18.4% each cover 2 of 10; 30.2% on the bottom, in NUMBERS 8u, covers 5 of 10; reproduced); use only beside row 4, since the class is the wrong size.

Wed 18 Nov: 3e; four of the ten, not five, sit at 27.6%-33.6% (Kaohsiung, Weiwuying, TPAC, TMC); that band sits near Q5d's small classes' 80th percentile (about 27%-37%), not a middle-to-high band; say it is the landmark class (row 4) beside the dollar gaps.

Wed 18 Nov: 3e; keep the size ratios (318 and about 1,850 times NT$3.77m, reproduced); drop all ten let at the lowest price (not shown per building) and supplementary budgets with no cap (row 7: a council cut one to NT$1,000).

Wed 18 Nov: store correction; corrects H9-097, whose +76% set a NT$6.7bn total against NT$3.78bn of direct works; the Control Yuan's +29.6% from NT$5.37bn stands; a correction, not a twin, so H9-097 is superseded, not merged.

Wed 18 Nov: store, 3e background; fix the dates as written: the cheque bounced on 10 Nov 2016 and the re-let in split, cut-down lots came in 2018; 4,351 over 3,706 days (1.17) reproduces; landmark causes only.
Wed 18 Nov: store, 3b background; landmark fee bills paid two years after opening; the half kept stays hers after 2033 (NUMBERS 4) and meets such a bill only by her choice, a limit, not a promise.

Wed 18 Nov: store; TMC's +33.6% reproduces; its lesson that a below-market works budget saves nothing is drawn from a big public landmark with an international tender, so say so; row 9 holds the diagnosis.

Wed 18 Nov: 3d; the Control Yuan quote stands, but fix the parallel: a pledge's risk is being stated too high, not low-balled, so say her figure is owned money, not an estimate; large public projects only, as its own column says.
Wed 18 Nov: store; Kaohsiung's +27.64% read at source (1,506.441 over 5,450 reproduces); adds the budget to store Q9-028's delay; class data for row 1.

Wed 18 Nov: Table 3/3e question, at what stage the co-sponsors' building budget was set; extends Q5-022's bands and Q5-021's stage point with a Taiwanese case; a monitoring question, never a trigger (CANON A34) or a budget of our own (case l.164-165).
Wed 18 Nov: store; the museum branch held its NT$6.0bn building budget and lost seven years; +32.2% on the whole plan reproduces; supports row 17's baseline point.

Wed 18 Nov: 3b illustration of D12 (fixed money, smaller design, later date); the NT$2.849bn is from an arts magazine only, and a national museum is a landmark, not her class; read at source and say the class before use.
Wed 18 Nov: 3e area 4; Taiwan's 2008 spike (8q's worst window ends Jul 2008, checked) hit an arts budget and then reversed; one public case with a price clause, as its own column says.
Wed 18 Nov: store; Liudui's +45.8% reproduces; beside the library's 0% it shows ten cases have no size pattern; opening year UNVERIFIED.
Wed 18 Nov: store correction; Q103-037's +14.7% is right only from the later NT$4.619bn baseline; +84.7% from the Oct 2016 total reproduces; not a twin, both stay with their baselines named.

Wed 18 Nov: 3b/3e presentation; name the baseline every time (hers is the stated top, 8q); use the Green Museumbrary and museum-branch pairs, since TPAC's +76% was a total set against direct works, a mix-up, not a choice of first budget; extends Q5-021.

Wed 18 Nov: store; +89.6% and the central share reproduce, but the NT$2,066.46m added back is not the whole NT$2,751m rise (3,070.6 plus 2,066.5 is 5,137.1); write that with other additions the total reached NT$5,822m.
Wed 18 Nov: Table 3/3e question, what was left out to make the co-sponsors' budget fit (減項發包, Taoyuan and TPAC at source); a monitoring question, never a budget of our own (case l.164-165).

Wed 18 Nov: 3b/3d; 44.8% to 23.6% reproduces, but the parallel breaks: Laura founds the residency (Q11e: the founder pays first), so she is nearer the city as owner, and legislators did press the fixed funder; say a top-up needed a new decision, never that nothing fell on it.

Wed 18 Nov: 3b; right that claim 3 overstated the other funders, but the owner may be Laura (Q11e); write that an overrun falls on the project's budget (scope, phasing, more raised), never on her stated contribution, and on her flexibility only by her choice (D12); grant rules as practice, never Taiwan law (case l.168-169).

Wed 18 Nov: 3e/Table 3; her payments and contribution are owned and dated, so a late building moves neither; the delay evidence is big public buildings plus one mid-size museum, so say so, never close to universal for a residency; extends store Q9-028.
Wed 18 Nov: 3e area 4; PCC 2024 data, small contracts got additions less often (15.66% against 22.15%; 1.41 and 1.93 reproduce); public contracts, measured against the award.

Wed 18 Nov: 3e area 4; the nearest Taiwanese class: small contracts add by more when they add (35.14% at 20% or more, 1,589 of 4,522 reproduces), matching Q5d's English and Norwegian finding; against the award, with the Budget Center's denominator caveat.

Wed 18 Nov: 3e area 4; about 1 small public contract in 18 added a fifth or more in 2024 (1,589 of 28,875; all six shares reproduce); one year, against the award; say it plainly, without the tail-and-middle phrase.
Wed 18 Nov: store, 3e; one township's small works changed in 64.5% of cases (98 of 152 reproduces) and added about 21%, owner causes the largest part; abstract only, base of the 21% unclear.

Wed 18 Nov: 3b/3e; owner's changed needs as the largest cause (39.80% of 98) stands; 1,183 days on 615 is 192.4%, not 193.30% (that needs 612 days), so re-read before use; large public contracts, as its column says.

Wed 18 Nov: store; a mid-size public museum (NT$245m, about 65 times her NT$3.77m) lost three-plus years to decisions, not builders; partly secondary; a council cut, never framed as arts money cut in a recession.
Wed 18 Nov: store; the same failure modes at NT$190m public heritage scale (about 50 times her NT$3.77m), no overrun figure; pairs with Q5d row 25.
Wed 18 Nov: 3e; say the class leans high whenever row 1 is used (the LY table lists only plans revised twice or by 40% or more, quote at source).
Wed 18 Nov: 3e area 4; never add the class to 8q's 28.0% (checked): a decade of NT$ budget change already holds price rises that a two-year US-dollar move counts; prevents double counting.
Wed 18 Nov: store; film centre phase 2 +84.1% reproduces (approved 6 Jul 2026); unfinished, outside the ten; a news report only.
Wed 18 Nov: 3e; Taiwan's own legislature asked its culture ministry to plan from past arts buildings (quote at source); a method echo for the class view, never an estimate of her building.
